---
title: "Rust library"
---

This document describes the design of the Rust library and of the individual CLI
commands, as well as tracks the implementation status. This document is split
into the functions for the CLI and the library implementing the CLI.

{{< include /docs/includes/_design-status.qmd >}}

The shapes, fill colours, and bolding of the boxes in the diagrams below have
specific meanings.

- All parallelograms are all input or output.
- Light gray parallelograms with bold edges are input arguments.
- Rectangular boxes are actions or processes, such as a function.
- Cylindrical boxes are internal types, such as Rust structs.
- Diamond boxes are decision points that represent "if" conditions.

## CLI code

All the CLI functions take one argument: `args`. The type of the `args` depends
on the function name, but their struct type is always the function name with
`Args` as the suffix (e.g. `ListArgs`). These structs are created when Rust
parses the command when it is used on the CLI.

Many functions or methods return a `Result` type. In those cases, the design
diagrams assume that the error will contain the correct message and be send to
`stderr`. So arrows and boxes are not included for errors to simplify the
diagrams.

The `init` CLI command isn't shown here as it is a very simple command to create
an `.zenodo.toml` file with empty `Metadata` fields.

### {{< var wip >}} `discard()` {#cli-discard}

This relatively simple function, like [`get()`](#cli-get), has an internal
`discard_deposit()` method that is used in other CLI functions. However, unlike
`get_deposit()` that requires a bit more steps, the [discard Zenodo
API](https://developers.zenodo.org/#discard) request used in `discard_deposit()`
is a (mostly) simple `POST` request to the `discard` endpoint.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-discard-cli
%%| fig-cap: "The flow of input and output through the `discard()` CLI function."
%%| fig-alt: >-
%%|   Diagram showing the flow of input and output through the CLI function.

flowchart TD
    sandbox[/"--sandbox"/]:::inputs
    metadata_file[/"[metadata-file]"/]:::inputs
    token["get_token()"]
    session[("Session::new()")]
    read_metadata["read_metadata()"]
    metadata[("Metadata {...}")]
    require_deposit["require_deposit()"]
    is_draft["is_draft()"]
    discard_deposit["discard_deposit()"]
    output[/"Message<br>or nothing<br>(stdout)"/]

    decision_draft{"draft?"}

    metadata_file -->
      read_metadata -->
      metadata -->|add ID| session

    session --> discard_deposit

    sandbox & token -->
      session -->
      require_deposit -->
      is_draft --> decision_draft
      decision_draft -->|true| discard_deposit -->
      output

    decision_draft -->|false| output

    classDef inputs fill:lightgray,stroke-width:3px
```

### {{< var wip >}} `sync()` {#cli-sync}

Because of the wide variety of potential output formats, the internals of this
function need to be flexible to adding new formats. It makes heavy use of traits
and generics in `impl` methods in Rust to keep a simple flow. Methods of the
traits are applied to each of the formats structs, e.g. for `CitationCff` or
`ZenodoJson`.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-sync-cli
%%| fig-cap: >-
%%|   The flow of input and output through the `sync()` CLI function. 'New'
%%|   metadata synced to a format is joined with the 'old' metadata in that
%%|   format.
%%| fig-alt: >-
%%|   Diagram showing the flow of input and output from input to output. There
%%|   are various shapes for each box, which is described at the top of the
%%|   document.

flowchart TD
    metadata_file[/"[metadata-file]"/]
    to[/"--to"/]

    read_metadata["read_metadata()"]
    metadata[("Metadata {...}")]
    formats[("ToFormats<br>enum")]
    sync_format["sync_format()<br>method"]
    output[/"Updated<br>format file"/]

    metadata_file -->
      read_metadata -->
      metadata -->
      sync_format

    to -->
      formats -->|match to<br>correct<br>format struct| sync_format -->
      output
```

## Library code

`enum ToFormats`

:   This `enum` contains a listing of all the different the different formats we
    sync to as received from the `--to` arg, as listed in the
    [CLI](cli.qmd#cli-sync) page.

`trait from(metadata: &Metadata) -> Self`

:   This uses the built-in `From` trait to build
    [`from()`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/convert/trait.From.html) `impl`
    methods on the different format structs. For example, for `CitationCff` it
    could be `impl From<&Metadata> for CitationCff`.

`Metadata {...}`

:   This contains the metadata from the Zenodo TOML file, e.g. `.zenodo.toml`.
    Will eventually form the deposit's
    [`metadata`](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#depositions) field.

`read_metadata(path: &Path) -> Result<Metadata, Error>`

:   Reads the Zenodo TOML file, e.g. `.zenodo.toml`.

### `sync_format()`

This generic function operates on the various format structs, e.g.
`CitationCff`. It is a simple convenience method for use in the `match` arms of
the `sync()` CLI command. It is a thin wrapper around `from()`, `read()`,
`left_join()`, and `write()`. The signature is:

```rust
fn sync_format<T>(metadata: &Metadata) -> Result<(), Error>;
```

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-sync-format
%%| fig-cap: >-
%%|   The flow of input and output through the helper `sync_format()` CLI
%%|   function. 'New' metadata synced to a format is joined with the 'old'
%%|   metadata in that format.
%%| fig-alt: >-
%%|   Diagram showing the flow of input and output from input to output. There
%%|   are various shapes for each box, which is described at the top of the
%%|   document.

flowchart TD
    metadata[("Metadata {...}")]
    from["from()<br>trait"]

    subgraph new_format ["Format structs (new)"]
      %% Fix positions with hidden arrows
      citation_cff[("CitationCff {...}")] ~~~
        pyproject_toml[("PyprojectToml {...}")]
      zenodo_json[("ZenodoJson {...}")] ~~~
        codemeta_json[("CodemetaJson {...}")]
      quarto_yml[("QuartoYml {...}")] ~~~
        description_r[("DescriptionR {...}")]
    end

    old_format[("Format structs (old)")]

    left{"left?"}
    right{"right?"}

    left_join["left_join()<br>trait"]
    read["read()<br>trait"]
    write["write()<br>trait"]

    metadata -->
      from -->
      new_format

    new_format -->
      read -->
      old_format -->
      right

    new_format -->
      left

    left & right -->
      left_join -->
      write

    new_format:::inner
    classDef inner fill:none
```

`Deposit {...}`

:   A struct that represents the JSON response received from Zenodo. Mainly
    needed for updating the `deposit.metadata` object and for the `deposit.id`
    fields. The Zenodo deposit fields are listed on
    [Zenodo](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#entities). Some fields are not
    converted from the Zenodo JSON representation to our `Deposit` struct as
    they aren't needed by zen-do nor needed during communication with the Zenodo
    API. Specifically `doi_url`, `created`, `modified`, and `title` are not
    kept.

`enum Formats`

:   This `enum` contains all the different formats we sync to, as listed in the
    [CLI](cli.qmd#cli-convert) page.

`get_token(sandbox: bool) -> Result<String, Error>`

:   As described in the [CLI](cli.qmd) page, this gets the token from either the
    keyring or from the env variables.

`Metadata {...}`

:   This contains the metadata from the Zenodo TOML file, i.e., `.zenodo.toml`.
    It will eventually form the deposit's
    [`metadata`](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#depositions) field.

`Metadata::into_format(self: Self, to: Formats) -> T`

:   This `impl` [generic
    method](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rust-by-example/generics/impl.html) on
    `Metadata` converts the `Metadata` struct into the selected `to` format
    using the `Formats` enum. The `T` type is any of the output structs, like
    `CitationCff`, `ZenodoJson`, or `PyprojectToml`.

`read_metadata(path: &Path) -> Result<Metadata, Error>`

:   Reads the Zenodo TOML file, e.g. `.zenodo.toml`.

`Session {header, url, connection, zendo_id, deposit}`

:   The struct acts as a container to hold everything necessary for all the
    various functions that it is used by. It contains the information needed to
    connect to Zenodo, to send a request, as well as the details from the
    request. This object is used with
    [reqwest](https://docs.rs/reqwest/latest/reqwest/) to build and send the
    request to the [Zenodo API](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#rest-api).
    Since `zen-do` doesn't send many requests to Zenodo and because the requests
    are fairly simple, they are sent synchronously. That way we don't need to
    set up any `async` structures. The `connection` field will hold the
    `reqwest::blocking::Client::new()` object, where `blocking` is what sets the
    synchronous connection. The fields `zendo_id` and `deposit` are `Option`
    types.

`Session::discard_deposit(self: mut self) -> Result<Self, Error>`

:   This `impl` method on `Session` sends a
    [discard](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#discard) request to Zenodo.
    If the request succeeds, the `Session.deposit` field is set to `None`. If
    the current deposit on Zenodo needs to be retrieved, do `Session::new()`
    again to start over.

`Session::require_deposit(self: &self) -> Result<Self, Error>`

:   A simple `impl` method on `Session` to ensure that the `Session` has a
    `deposit` field. Used for CLI commands that require a `deposit` be present.

<!-- TODO: Unsure if this should be a `Result` type instead... -->

`Session::is_draft(self: &self) -> bool`

:   Checks the
    [`deposit.state`](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#representation) field
    if it is "inprogress", or if the `state` is not "error" and the
    `deposit.submitted` field is false. Is an `impl` method on `Session`.

`Session::new(sandbox, token, zendo_id)`

:   This constructs a new `Session` struct with details needed for reqwest to
    correctly send a request to Zenodo. Based on the `sandbox` value, the `url`
    field will point to either `sandbox.zenodo.org` or `zenodo.org` URLs. If the
    `zendo_id` is given, a request will be sent to Zenodo for the deposit
    connected to the ID, the response of which will be attached to the `deposit`
    field to limit repeated requests. Importantly, the main purpose for getting
    and assigning the `deposit` at this point is to get the Zenodo identifier in
    [`deposit.id`](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#entities). When using
    `new()`, the `reqwest::blocking::Client::new()` will be added to
    `connection` to reuse that object for each request sent to Zenodo. The
    `token` will be added to the header, which will be added to the `reqwest`
    connection field.

`trait left_join(self, right: Option<Self>) -> Self`

:   This trait will be used to create methods on all of the different format
    structs. This allows a variety of formats (e.g. `CitationCff`) to be used
    without writing new code for each of those formats. Left join means that all
    the fields in the left hand side (`self`) are kept and any that are missing
    from the right hand side (`right`) are merged into it. This enables any
    values added to an existing file, e.g. `CITATION.cff`, to be kept when
    joined over. If nothing exists on the right side, the left side is output
    without any changes.

`trait const PATH: &Path`

:   This [associated
    constant](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/associated-items.html)
    as a trait applied to the different format structs is used internally in
    `read()` and `write()` to point to the correct locations of the output
    format types. For example, with the enum `ToFormat::CitationCff`, the path
    to this file should be `CITATION.cff`, in the same folder as where the
    `metadata-file` is found.

`trait read() -> Result<Option<Self>, Error>`

:   Like `left_join()` above, this trait as an `impl` method on the format
    structs reads any existing file that is present. If no file is present, it
    will output `None`. Uses the `PATH` const to read the right path location.

`trait write(self) -> Result<(), Error>`

:   Like `left_join()` and `read()` above, this trait as an `impl` method on the
    format structs writes the format to any file. It uses the `PATH` const. It
    will overwrite the contents of the file, though with `left_join()` it will
    maintain any details not found in the `Metadata`.

`ZendoId`

:   This type contains the `zendo_id` value from the Zenodo TOML file, e.g.
    `.zenodo.toml`.
